# Manifest Field Reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask emit-schemas` from the `DatasetSpec` JSON Schema. Do not edit. -->

Every field of the dataset manifest, generated from its JSON Schema. The prose chapter [The Dataset Manifest](manifest.md) explains how the pieces fit together; this page is the exhaustive list. The schema itself is `app/src/schemas/dataset_spec.json` in the repository, and the desktop app builds its manifest form from it.

Paths in a manifest are relative to the directory that holds it unless they are absolute. A field marked *required* has no default and must be present; an optional field may be omitted.

## DatasetSpec

Top-level dataset manifest. Authoritative description of where the user's calibration data lives and how to interpret it.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cameras` | array of [CameraSource](#camerasource) | yes | | Per-camera image sources. Length must match the topology's expected camera count (a single-camera topology requires exactly one entry, a rig topology at least two). |
| `target` | [TargetSpec](#targetspec) | yes | | Calibration-target specification. Tagged enum on `kind`. |
| `topology` | [Topology](#topology) | yes | | Calibration topology — selects which problem type the runner will dispatch to. |
| `_unresolved` | array of string | no | | Field paths the manifest generator could not determine. Validated to be empty before the runner accepts the manifest. Populated as e.g. `["pose_convention.transform"]`. |
| `description` | string | no | | Free-form human-readable description. |
| `detector` | [DetectorSpec](#detectorspec) | no | | Detector-stage overrides shared by target families. Defaults preserve the detector's built-in behavior. |
| `laser` | [LaserExtractionSpec](#laserextractionspec) | no | | Laser-line extraction parameters for the laser topologies. `None` means defaults — extraction tuning has safe defaults and is not a fail-fast ambiguity. Rejected on non-laser topologies. |
| `pose_convention` | [PoseConvention](#poseconvention) | no | | Frame conventions for robot poses. **No defaults** — every component is required when `robot_poses` is set. |
| `pose_pairing` | [PosePairing](#posepairing) | no | | How per-camera images are paired across views (and optionally with robot poses). `None` is permitted only where pairing is irrelevant: a single camera without robot poses. |
| `robot_poses` | [RobotPoseSource](#robotposesource) | no | | Robot-pose source for hand-eye topologies. `None` for pure-intrinsics calibrations. |
| `upstream_calibration` | string | no | | Path to a frozen upstream `RigHandeyeExport` JSON, relative to the manifest directory unless absolute. Required for `Topology::RigLaserlineDevice`, rejected elsewhere. Joint hand-eye laserline calibration computes its own hand-eye warm start and does not use this field. |
| `version` | integer | no | `1` | Format-version sentinel. Always `1` for now; bumped on breaking schema revisions. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## CameraSource

Per-camera image source.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Stable camera identifier (e.g. `"cam0"`). Used as a key in pose pairings and downstream exports. |
| `images` | [ImagePattern](#imagepattern) | yes | Glob pattern (e.g. `"cam0/*.png"`) or explicit list of image paths, relative to the manifest's directory unless absolute. |
| `laser_images` | [ImagePattern](#imagepattern) | no | Laser-frame image source for the laser topologies. One laser image per view, captured by the same sensor with the line projector on; `roi_xywh` applies to laser frames too. Laser images pair with target views through `pose_pairing`. |
| `roi_xywh` | array of 4 integer | no | Optional rectangular ROI in source-image pixels — `[x, y, w, h]`. When set, only the cropped region is fed to the detector and stored in the export's image manifest. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## ImagePattern

How image paths for a camera are listed.

Tagged on `kind`; the fields depend on the variant.

**`kind = "glob"`**: Single shell-glob pattern, evaluated relative to the manifest directory. Example: `"cam0/*.png"`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string | yes | The glob pattern. |

**`kind = "list"`**: Explicit ordered list of paths.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | array of string | yes | Paths relative to the manifest directory unless absolute. |

## TargetSpec

Calibration-target metadata. Tagged on `kind`.

Tagged on `kind`; the fields depend on the variant.

**`kind = "chessboard"`**: Standard checkerboard. Counts are interior corners (i.e. `9x6` ⇒ a 10×7 black-and-white square grid).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | integer | yes | Number of interior corners along the cols axis. |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Number of interior corners along the rows axis. |
| `square_size_m` | number | yes | Edge length of one square in metres. |

**`kind = "charuco"`**: ChArUco board. Marker IDs and dictionary live here so detection is fully deterministic from the manifest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | integer | yes | Number of squares along the cols axis. |
| `dictionary` | string | yes | ArUco dictionary identifier (e.g. `"DICT_4X4_50"`). The detector validates this against the supported set. |
| `marker_size_m` | number | yes | Edge length of an embedded marker in metres. |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Number of squares along the rows axis (full grid, not interior corners). |
| `square_size_m` | number | yes | Edge length of one square in metres. |

**`kind = "puzzleboard"`**: Puzzleboard target: a self-identifying chessboard. The layout name carries the board's dimensions, so the manifest fully determines detection.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cell_size_m` | number | yes | Edge length of one cell in metres. |
| `layout` | string | yes | Board dimensions as `puzzle_<rows>x<cols>` (e.g. `"puzzle_12x12"`; the `puzzle_` prefix is optional). |

**`kind = "ringgrid"`**: Coded ring-grid target (the `ringgrid` crate). The board is a hex-lattice of self-identifying ring markers; its geometry mirrors `ringgrid::BoardLayout` so the manifest fully determines detection.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `long_row_cols` | integer | yes | Number of columns in the longest (even-indexed) row. Shorter rows are derived by the hex-lattice layout. |
| `marker_inner_radius_m` | number | yes | Inner ring radius in metres. |
| `marker_outer_radius_m` | number | yes | Outer ring radius in metres. |
| `marker_ring_width_m` | number | yes | Width of each ring band in metres. |
| `pitch_m` | number | yes | Center-to-center spacing between adjacent markers in metres. |
| `rows` | integer | yes | Number of marker rows. |

## Topology

Calibration topology — selects the problem-type dispatch.

A topology describes the data (how many cameras, robot poses, laser images), not the camera model: a tilted (Scheimpflug) single camera is a `planar_intrinsics` dataset whose calibration config names the sensor.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `planar_intrinsics` | Single camera, planar target — `PlanarIntrinsicsProblem` (any camera model, including a tilted sensor). |
| `single_cam_handeye` | Single camera mounted on a robot — `SingleCamHandeyeProblem`. |
| `laserline_device` | Camera + laser plane — `LaserlineDeviceProblem`. |
| `rig_extrinsics` | Multi-camera rig, target only — `RigExtrinsicsProblem`. |
| `rig_handeye` | Multi-camera rig + robot — `RigHandeyeProblem`. |
| `rig_handeye_laserline` | Multi-camera rig + robot + laser planes — joint hand-eye/laser BA. |
| `rig_laserline_device` | Multi-camera rig + laser planes — `RigLaserlineDeviceProblem`. |

## DetectorSpec

Target-detector overrides. These options affect feature detection only; they are hashed into the detection-cache key by the runner.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chess_corners` | [ChessCornersDetectorSpec](#chesscornersdetectorspec) | no | ChESS corner extractor options shared by chessboard-like detectors (plain chessboard and ChArUco). |
| `min_features_per_view` | integer | no | Minimum detected features for a view (or a camera's slot in a rig view) to be kept, in every topology. `None` keeps the runner default (4, the homography minimum). Raise it for detectors whose sparse detections are unreliable — e.g. ring-grid decodes with < 8 markers are noisy enough to poison a solve. Set it to a plain chessboard's corner count (`rows × cols`) to keep only complete boards: rig and hand-eye views share one target frame, and a partial chessboard is labelled from its own top-left corner. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## ChessCornersDetectorSpec

ChESS corner extractor overrides.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_corner_strength` | number | no | Minimum corner strength for a detected corner to enter the grid builder. `None` keeps the detector default (`33.0`). The floor is on the strategy's response scale; under Radon the default never binds.<br><br>The default drops weakly-firing corners, which is the right trade whenever corners are plentiful. Set `0.0` to disable it on small or soft image tiles, where the floor can remove a third of the board and the resulting sparse view conditions worse than the weak corners did. |
| `strategy` | [CornerStrategySpec](#cornerstrategyspec) | no | Corner detector. `None` keeps ChESS. |
| `threshold_value` | number | no | Acceptance threshold on the corner response. `None` keeps the strategy's default.<br><br>Under ChESS it is an absolute floor on the raw response: a corner is kept when its response exceeds it. Under Radon it is a fraction in `(0, 1]` of the frame's maximum response.<br><br>A sibling `threshold_mode` key is rejected by `deny_unknown_fields`: the corner detector has no threshold mode. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## CornerStrategySpec

The corner detector a chessboard-like detector runs.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `chess` | The ChESS response. Fast; the default. |
| `radon` | The whole-image Radon response. Several times slower than ChESS, and less biased at a corner's sub-pixel position on sharp, finely sampled boards (e.g. rendered ones). |

## LaserExtractionSpec

Laser-line extraction parameters. Consumed by the runner's injected `LaserPixelExtractor`; hashed (canonical JSON) into the detection-cache key so edits re-extract.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min_points` | integer | no | `20` | Minimum extracted points for a usable laser view. Views below the bar are dropped (single camera) or become gap slots (rig). Must be at least 2 (a line needs two points); 0/1 would let an empty extraction pass as usable and leave the plane unconstrained. |
| `neg_thresh` | number | no | `4.0` | Negative-edge response threshold. |
| `pos_thresh` | number | no | `4.0` | Positive-edge response threshold. |
| `scan_axis` | [LaserScanAxis](#laserscanaxis) | no | `"cols"` | Scan direction. `cols` walks image columns (one point per column; for laser lines running mostly left-to-right), `rows` walks image rows. |
| `sigma` | number | no | `1.2` | Gaussian derivative sigma in pixels for the edge detector. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## LaserScanAxis

Laser scan direction.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `cols` | One detection per image column. |
| `rows` | One detection per image row. |

## PoseConvention

Frame conventions for the robot pose stream.

All three components are required (no defaults). Each is a closed enum so the runtime supports a finite, validated set of conventions.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rotation_format` | [RotationFormat](#rotationformat) | yes | How rotation is parameterised in the file. |
| `transform` | [TransformConvention](#transformconvention) | yes | Which transform the pose row encodes. |
| `translation_units` | [TranslationUnits](#translationunits) | yes | Translation units in the file. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## RotationFormat

Rotation parameterisation in the file.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `quat_xyzw` | Hamilton quaternion as `[qx, qy, qz, qw]`. |
| `quat_wxyz` | Hamilton quaternion as `[qw, qx, qy, qz]`. |
| `euler_xyz_deg` | Intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in degrees. |
| `euler_xyz_rad` | Intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in radians. |
| `euler_zyx_deg` | Intrinsic ZYX Euler angles in degrees. |
| `euler_zyx_rad` | Intrinsic ZYX Euler angles in radians. |
| `axis_angle_rad` | Axis-angle vector (length encodes magnitude, radians). |
| `matrix4x4_row_major` | Row-major 4×4 homogeneous matrix flattened across 16 columns. |

## TransformConvention

Which transform a pose row encodes.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `t_base_tcp` | `T_base_tcp` — gripper pose in the robot base frame (KUKA, UR default). |
| `t_tcp_base` | `T_tcp_base` — base pose in the gripper frame (some ABB exports). |
| `t_world_tcp` | `T_world_tcp` — gripper pose in a fixed world frame (less common; some lab-frame setups). |
| `t_tcp_world` | `T_tcp_world` — world pose in the gripper frame. |

## TranslationUnits

Translation units in the file.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `m` | Metres (SI, preferred). |
| `mm` | Millimetres (some ABB / Fanuc exports). |

## PosePairing

How per-camera image lists align across views and (optionally) align with robot poses.

Tagged on `kind`; the fields depend on the variant.

**`kind = "by_index"`**: All cameras have the same number of images, paired by index (`image[i]` from cam0 ↔ `image[i]` from cam1 ↔ `pose[i]`).

**`kind = "shared_filename_token"`**: A regex applied to filenames extracts a shared "view token" (e.g. timestamp or pose id). All cameras and the pose file must produce the same set of tokens.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | string | yes | Name of the capture group whose value identifies the view. |
| `regex` | string | yes | Regex with at least one named capture group. |

## RobotPoseSource

Where and how robot poses are stored on disk.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | [RobotPoseFormat](#robotposeformat) | yes | File-format selector. |
| `path` | string | yes | Path to the pose file, relative to the manifest directory unless absolute. |
| `columns` | [PoseColumnMap](#posecolumnmap) | no | Column / field mapping from the user's file to the canonical fields the converter consumes. Required for the tabular formats (`csv` / `json` / `jsonl`) unless `matrix_field` is set; must be absent for `rowmajor4x4` and `counted4x4`, whose matrix layout is fixed. |
| `matrix_field` | string | no | For `json` / `jsonl` files whose rows store the whole pose as a single nested 4×4 (or flat-16) array field, names that field (e.g. `"tcp2base"`). Mutually exclusive with `columns`; requires `pose_convention.rotation_format = matrix4x4_row_major`. Translation comes from the matrix's fourth column, scaled by `translation_units`. No `pose_id` ⇒ `by_index` pairing only. |

Unknown fields are rejected.

## RobotPoseFormat

Robot-pose file format.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `csv` | Comma-separated values with a header row. |
| `json` | JSON array of objects. |
| `jsonl` | JSONL (one JSON object per line). |
| `rowmajor4x4` | Headerless text: each non-empty line is 16 whitespace-separated floats forming a row-major 4×4 homogeneous transform (KUKA-style exports). Requires `pose_convention.rotation_format = "matrix4x4_row_major"` and no `columns` mapping. |
| `counted4x4` | Headerless text: the matrix count, then that many row-major 4×4 homogeneous transforms as whitespace-separated floats on any number of lines (the layout of the robot-world hand-eye datasets of Tabb and Ahmad Yousef). Same requirements as `rowmajor4x4`. |

## PoseColumnMap

Mapping from user-defined column / field names to the canonical pose fields. All seven of `tx, ty, tz, qx, qy, qz, qw` are required when `rotation_format` is a quaternion; the runner rejects partial mappings as a fail-fast event.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rotation` | array of string | yes | Rotation columns. Length and meaning depend on the `pose_convention.rotation_format`. |
| `tx` | string | yes | Translation x column. |
| `ty` | string | yes | Translation y column. |
| `tz` | string | yes | Translation z column. |
| `pose_id` | string | no | Optional view-id column (string or integer). When absent, the pose row index is used as the implicit pose id. |

Unknown fields are rejected.
